why: Restores the guard the current shape deliberately replaced -- skipping the scale term under reduced motion instead of writing a rest scale -- which blocked-fire-ring.test.ts names as its negative control in prose; this entry is what makes that prose executable. The defect is only reachable when the preference flips MID-FLIGHT: the ring freezes at whatever scale it had reached and sits visibly oversized for the rest of its life instead of closing onto the hull. `reduced motion keeps the cue but removes the travel` sets the preference BEFORE spawning and so stays green under it, which is precisely why one case is not enough here; only `snaps an ALREADY-AIRBORNE ring to rest when reduced motion turns on mid-flight` fails. Same policy as death-ring-ignores-the-reduced-motion-policy, pinning the live toggle that entry's effect does not have. Scoped to blocked-fire-ring.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
